title: Concurrent context coalescer and tracing handoff for low-overhead SDKs
creator: Maya Chen
description: Context propagation in high-concurrency worker pools is causing large, frequent header churn and backpressure spikes. This ticket introduces a lightweight coalescer in the SDK and middleware that merges concurrent context mutations into a single, compact propagation envelope before the outbound carrier is written. Goal is to reduce header count/size and lower request tail latency without breaking existing trace continuity or baggage semantics.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes a concurrent-safe coalescer API that middleware can call before serialization
End-to-end traces remain contiguous across async boundaries in 100% of integration tests
Median outbound header size for high-concurrency synthetic workload reduced by >= 40% compared to baseline
p99 request tail latency improves by at least 10ms under the benchmark harness used by observability-team/perf-dashboard
Compatibility mode for consumers that require raw per-change headers (toggleable via env var)
Automated fuzz tests for out-of-order mutation and duplicate writes included in the suite
Docs and examples added to SDK README and Console instrumentation guide
implementation_notes: Introduce per-request coalescer object attached to request context; coalescer accumulates mutation deltas and produces a single serialized envelope on flush
Use versioned tombstones to ensure last-writer-wins semantics without global locks; apply atomic compare-and-swap for edge cases
Serialization format: compact header with base64-encoded delta list; fall back to existing headers if downstream indicates incompatibility
Expose middleware shim for Node and Go SDKs; implement a minimal C API for edge runtime integrations
Add nonblocking backoff: if coalescer is contended for >5ms, skip coalescing and write best-effort header to avoid latency amplification
Limit envelope length to 6KB by default with configurable threshold; truncate low-priority baggage entries when threshold exceeded
Instrument metrics: coalescer_flushes, coalescer_skips, coalescer_bytes_saved; add dashboards for these in console-observability project
Add integration test harness that spins up high-concurrency worker pool (500 concurrent requests) and measures header churn and tail latency
